subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency & streaming UX requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency & streaming UX requirements

Alex thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of pain and goals
- Pain: Your real-time transaction monitoring UI is sensitive to tail latency; users notice slow completion when the assistant streams longer summaries. Current p95 latency target is <= 350ms for short completions, and <= 800ms for streaming sessions.
- Current stack: Finly uses a mix of in-house microservices + an internal LLM endpoint (self-hosted) for summarization. They currently batch requests and route via an API gateway; concurrency spikes during batch settlement windows.
- Business goal: Reduce perceived streaming latency (improve streaming UX) while supporting burst concurrency up to ~800 concurrent sessions during peak. Cost per 1M tokens matters but can be traded for latency for core flows.

Success criteria we discussed
- p95 non-streaming inference <= 350ms for sub-512 token prompts
- p95 streaming incremental chunk latency <= 200ms for first N chunks (smooth UX)
- Support sustained concurrency of ~400 sessions and burst to ~800 for 5-10 minute windows
- No regression in output quality for summary tasks (maintain current ROUGE-style baseline they run internally)

Open technical notes (from our call)
- Finly currently uses batching with max batch size ~64 which helps throughput but increases tail latency during low QPS.
- They are seeing KV-cache warm-up costs on cold sessions and warm-start jitter for streaming.
- Network hop counts: multiple internal proxies add ~40-80ms in some paths.

Proposed next steps
1) Aditya to send a short perf questionnaire to capture model sizes, average tokens per request, and current concurrency patterns. (See attached xlsx)
2) Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with Finly infra + product (suggested: Thu 18 Jun, 10am PT).
3) Run a short, scoped POC: Redwood-hosted test endpoints + streaming profile for a week to collect p95 numbers under controlled load.

Attachments: redwood_perf_qs.xlsx (short questionnaire), network-requirements.pdf (helpful checklist)

If any of this looks off or you want to add detail, reply inline and we’ll update. Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole

marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 16:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 latency & streaming UX requirements

Marissa — thanks for the clean recap, looks right to me. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Target clarification: The 350ms p95 is for single-shot UI calls (search/short-summary). For streaming, the main complaint is long pauses between chunks — we want chunk latency consistent and first-byte under 150-200ms if possible.
- Concurrency: 400 sustained is a good number; bursts can hit ~900 but that’s short (3-7 minutes) during settlement windows.
- Models: We currently run a mix of a 7B finetuned model and a 13B for long-form. For POC we can route short summaries to the 7B.

We’re available for Thu 18 Jun 10am PT. Priya (product) will join the deep-dive. Looking forward to the perf questionnaire.

Thanks,
Alex
Senior Product Manager, Finly
alex.johnson@finly.com

Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood perf questionnaire + a few technical Qs

Alex / Priya — attaching a concise perf questionnaire that will help us size a scoped POC and provision test capacity. A few technical items to call out here: 

1) Can you share typical token distribution (median, 75p, 95p) for the summary calls and streaming sessions?
2) For streaming, what is your chunking strategy (tokens per chunk, time-based flush, or hybrid)?
3) Do you have server-side keepalive or connection pooling right now? If so, stats on average connection reuse per session would help.
4) Do you have any hard egress / networking constraints for traffic to a hosted Redwood endpoint? (we noted multi-hop proxies)

Attachment: redwood_perf_qs.xlsx (please fill and return; 6-8 fields)

Also, optional: if you can share a small trace (example request with timestamps) we can use to reproduce the tail in our test harness.

I’ll also prepare an initial config recommendation (batching, KV cache TTL, chunk size) ahead of the deep-dive so we can iterate.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
